headers.//: The CSP that counts. index.html carries the same policy in a <meta> tag, which browsers ignore for frame-ancestors (and which cannot be relied on generally), so this header is what actually protects the portal. connect-src names the two origins the app talks to instead of all of https:, because the admin's access and refresh tokens live in localStorage (supabase-js persistSession) and a blanket https: would let injected script post them anywhere. Update the two hosts if the Supabase project or the API domain changes.
headers.value: default-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://chvibqjstucybirsmpwu.supabase.co wss://chvibqjstucybirsmpwu.supabase.co https://studia-api-mu.vercel.app; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'

headers.//: frame-ancestors above covers modern browsers; this is the older equivalent and costs nothing. Without either, an admin action such as deleting a user can be clickjacked through an iframe.
A private portal has no business being indexed, and the meta tag only reaches crawlers that render HTML.
Nothing in the portal uses these.
